title: Prompt-Pay Discounts on Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility Accounts
content:
**Statement terms and system card — prompt-pay discount, Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility.**

## The policy

Summit Ridge grants a prompt-pay discount on a coinsurance charge on the coverage account that a patient-payment entry pays in full on or after the latest statement issued on the account and no later than the class's prompt-pay window, in calendar days, after it, on a coverage class whose prompt-pay discount percentage is above 0. The discount is posted as one adjustment with the reason "prompt-pay discount" against the charge paid; a class whose prompt-pay discount percentage is 0 grants none.

- **Late posting.** A prompt-pay discount that was not posted on the paying day is posted when the omission is found before the account's next statement is issued. Once a later statement has gone out showing the account without it, the account stands as statemented and no discount is posted for that payment.
- **Order of working.** Missed prompt-pay discounts are worked one payment at a time, starting from the account's most recent patient-payment entry.
- **Other charges.** A prompt-pay discount on a charge other than a coinsurance charge remains under the base adjustment rule.
- **Beyond the open amount.** For a prompt-pay discount, and only for a prompt-pay discount, the adjustment is posted for its full figure even though the qualifying payment has already brought the charge's open amount to 0.00, the discount staying on the account as a credit toward its other open charges. Every adjustment other than a hardship or a prompt-pay discount remains under the base rule and never stacks beyond its charge's open amount.
- **Against a hardship discount.** When a hardship and a prompt-pay discount could both apply to one charge, only the larger is posted, with QMB protection displacing both.
- **No Medicaid record needed.** For a prompt-pay discount, and only for a prompt-pay discount, no Medicaid record has to be active, because the discount rests on the payment that earned it. QMB protection itself, and every adjustment other than a hardship or a prompt-pay discount, remains under the base rule, so QMB protection applies only while the Medicaid record carrying QMB status is in status active.

## Booking the discount: `apply_prompt_pay_discount_12f1a0eb`

**Capability.** The tool books a prompt-pay discount against one patient charge that the patient paid in full. One call writes one prompt-pay-discount adjustment entry dated today that points at the charge, and lowers the account's patient balance by the same amount; the patient sees the discount as a credit line under that charge on the account history.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `apply_prompt_pay_discount_12f1a0eb` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

- `coverage_id` — the reference number of the coverage account (the insurance coverage record on the patient's file) that carries the charge, as returned by the coverage lookup. Identifier.
- `applied_to_entry_id` — the reference number of the patient charge entry the discount belongs to, as returned by the patient-account ledger lookup for that account. Identifier.
- `amount` — the prompt-pay discount to book on the charge, in USD: a positive figure with 2 decimal places (cents), stored exactly as given, rounded half up to the cent.

**Return.** A text rendering of a record with `adjustment_id` (reference of the new prompt-pay-discount entry), `coverage_id` (the account adjusted), `applied_to_entry_id` (the charge credited), `amount` (USD, 2 decimals), `posting_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD), `patient_balance` (the balance once the discount is booked, USD, 2 decimals) and `status`, the string "booked". A receipt whose status is "booked" means the discount is on the account.

## Questions on the terms

**A coinsurance charge was paid in full within the window, the discount was not posted, and the next statement has since gone out without it. Is it still posted?** No — the account stands as statemented and no discount is posted for that payment.

**A payment made before the latest statement was issued — does it earn the discount?** No; the payment must be made on or after the latest statement.
